BEACH SAFETY
Red and yellow flags: lifeguarded area, swim between the flags.
Red flag: danger, do not enter the water.
Black and white chequered flags: zone for surfboards and kayaks.
Lifeguards on duty daily 10:00 to 18:00, 23 May to 27 September 2026.
In an emergency call 999 and ask for the Coastguard.

DANGER: FAST RISING TIDES
The causeway to Gull Rock is covered by the sea for approx. 4 hours around each high tide.
Check the tide table before crossing. Today's safe crossing times are shown on the board at the slipway.
Do not attempt to cross if water is over the path. Last year 37 people were rescued from this spot.
Sandmere Coastguard Rescue Team

DOGS ON THE BEACH
From 1 May to 30 September dogs are not permitted on Main Beach between the pier and the lifeguard tower.
Dogs are welcome all year on North Beach beyond groyne no. 14.
Please clean up after your dog. Maximum penalty £1,000.
Kittiwake Bay Town Council, Environmental Services 01632 960517

NOTICE
The end of the Albion Pier will be closed from Monday 14 September to Friday 2 October 2026 for repairs to the decking.
The amusement hall, café and toilets at the pier entrance stay open 9am to 9pm as usual.
Angling permits bought for these dates will be refunded at the kiosk.
We apologise for any inconvenience.

BOARDWALK RULES
Bicycles permitted 5:00 AM to 10:00 AM only, May 15 through September 15.
No glass containers. No alcohol. No fires.
Skateboards and scooters prohibited at all times.
Violations subject to fines of $50 to $250 per Ord. No. 2019-14.
Driftwood Beach Police Dept. non-emergency (843) 555-0118

SWIMMING POOL
Open daily 09:00 to 19:30, lifeguard on duty 10:00 to 18:00
Water temperature today 26 °C
Shower before entering. No diving: depth 1.20 m to 1.80 m.
Children under 12 must be with an adult at all times.
Sunbeds may not be reserved with towels before 09:00. Towels left unattended will be removed by staff.
Hotel Brisa del Mar, Reception ext. 9

MARINE PARADE NEWS & GIFTS
Summer opening hours
Mon to Sat 7am to 9pm
Sun 8am to 8pm
Buckets, spades and crabbing lines inside
Bait available: frozen squid and mackerel
Sorry, no more than 3 school children at a time

SEAFRONT CAR PARK CHARGES
Up to 1 hour £2.00
Up to 2 hours £3.60
Up to 4 hours £6.40

Overnight 8pm to 8am £3.00
Coaches: £25.00 per day, bays 41 to 46 only
Pay by coin, card or call 01632 960884 quoting location 4417
Charges apply every day including bank holidays.

JELLYFISH WARNING
Several Portuguese man o' war have been found on this beach since 8 August.
Do not touch them, even if they appear dead: the tentacles can still sting.
If stung, rinse with sea water, not fresh water, and seek first aid at the lifeguard hut.
Report sightings to the Beach Office on 01632 960305.

LOST CHILDREN POINT
If you become separated from your child, go straight to the Lifeguard Tower opposite the Clock Tower café.
Lost children will be taken there and looked after by staff.
Give each child a wristband with your mobile number: free from the tower or the Tourist Information Centre.
Open 10am to 6pm daily in July and August.

FIREWORKS ON THE BAY
Wednesdays 5, 12, 19 and 26 August 2026 at 9.45pm
Best viewed from the Esplanade and West Cliff gardens
The promenade between the pier and the bandstand will close to traffic from 8pm to 11pm.
Extra buses on route 5 until 11.30pm.
If the weather is poor, check our page after 4pm for a decision.

BATHING WATER QUALITY
Sandmere Main Beach: rated Excellent (2022 to 2025)
Short-term pollution may occur after heavy rain. Advice against bathing will be posted here when needed.
Latest sample taken 10/08/2026: E. coli 18 cfu/100ml, intestinal enterococci 9 cfu/100ml.
For daily updates text SANDMERE to 07700 900214.

CLOSED FOR THE SEASON
The Sandpiper Kiosk is now closed until the spring.
Thank you to all our customers for a fantastic 2026 summer: 41,000 ice creams served!
We reopen on Friday 2 April 2027 at 10am.
Gift vouchers can still be bought online or by calling 07700 900583.

RIP CURRENTS
If caught in a rip current, don't fight it. Swim parallel to the shore, then swim back at an angle.
If you can't escape, float or tread water and wave for help.
No lifeguard on duty after 5:30 PM or before 9:00 AM.
Beach access #22, mile marker 7.5
Emergency: 911

THE ALBION PIER
Opened on 21 June 1871, the Albion Pier originally stretched 1,140 feet into the bay and cost £23,000 to build. Paddle steamers called at its landing stage three times a day in summer, bringing day-trippers from as far as Penmorrow.
A storm in January 1953 destroyed the outer 300 feet, and the pier was shortened to its present 840 feet. The cast-iron kiosks at the entrance are original and were restored in 2009.
Admission to the pier is free; the arcade and rides are open from Easter to October.

What lives in a rock pool?
Look under seaweed and in shady cracks. You may find shore crabs, which can be green, orange or even purple, and grow up to 8cm across the shell. Beadlet anemones look like blobs of red jelly when the tide is out, but open up into a ring of up to 192 tentacles underwater.
Remember the rock pool code: lift rocks gently, put everything back where you found it, and never take living creatures home.

The 7.52 from Penmorrow was late, as it was every Saturday in August, and by the time Nell stepped onto the platform at Kittiwake Bay the sun was already high over the harbour.

A Short History of the Driftwood Beach Boardwalk
The first boardwalk, just 8 feet wide and 1 mile long, was built in 1896 so that hotel guests would not track sand into the lobbies. It was laid in sections and taken up every winter.
Today's boardwalk runs 2.6 miles from the Inlet to 27th Street and is 40 feet wide at its widest point. More than 4 million visitors walk it each year.
Tip: the boards are numbered every 100 feet, which makes them handy for meeting friends.

Coast Path Walk 3: Kittiwake Bay to Seal Point
Distance 4.2 miles (6.8 km) one way. Allow 2 1/2 hours. Moderate, with 2 steep climbs and 146 steps down to Porth Gull cove.
From the harbour, follow the acorn signs up Chapel Hill past the coastguard lookout. After 1.5 km the path levels out along the cliff top; look out for gannets diving and, from August, grey seal pups on the beach below.
Return by the land train from Seal Point (last train 17:45) or bus 5.

CALA SERENA
Once a quiet fishing village of 600 people, Cala Serena now welcomes some 250,000 visitors a year. The old town, with its whitewashed houses and the 16th-century Iglesia de San Telmo, sits on a headland between two beaches.
Playa de las Dunas, to the east, is long and sandy with lifeguards from June to September. Cala Chica, to the west, is a small cove reached by 84 steps and is popular with snorkellers.
Market day is Wednesday, 8:00 to 14:00, in the Plaza Mayor.

BATHING. Bathing is permitted from the machines on the South Sands between the hours of 6 a.m. and 8 p.m. Charges: bathing machine, 6d.; towel, 1d.; costume, 2d. Mixed bathing is allowed at the east end of the sands only.
The Corporation employs a boatman, who is in attendance during bathing hours. Visitors are earnestly requested not to bathe within one hour of a meal, nor to swim beyond the line of buoys.

Staying safe in the sun
The sun is strongest between 11am and 3pm from March to October. Spend time in the shade during these hours, especially with babies and young children.
Use a sunscreen of at least SPF 30 with 4 or 5 star UVA protection. Most people use too little: an adult needs about 6 to 8 teaspoons to cover the whole body.
Reapply every 2 hours and straight after swimming, even if the bottle says water resistant.
Drink plenty of water. A hat and sunglasses with the CE mark help too.

Pip the puffin lived on a rock called Little Teacup, 3 miles out to sea. Every morning she counted her brothers and sisters: 1, 2, 3, 4, and her, 5.
One stormy night, the wind blew so hard that when Pip woke up, she counted only 4. 'Where is Wren?' she cried. The waves were as tall as the lighthouse and the sky was the colour of porridge.
'Don't worry,' said Grandpa Puffin. 'We'll find her before the tide turns at half past 2.'

Sea Fishing from the Pier
Mackerel arrive in large numbers from late May. Use a string of 6 feathers and a 4 oz lead, cast as far as you can and retrieve with a jerky motion. On a good day you can fill a bucket in an hour, but please take only what you will eat.
Minimum sizes apply to many species: bass must be at least 42 cm and plaice 27 cm. Bass caught in February and March must be returned.
Night fishing on the Albion Pier is allowed on Fridays and Saturdays until 2am, permit required.

Hurricane Season: June 1 to November 30
If an evacuation order is issued for Seabright Shores, all visitors must leave the island. Follow the blue evacuation route signs to Highway 17; the drawbridge will lock down for outbound traffic only.
Your emergency kit should include water (1 gallon per person per day for at least 3 days), non-perishable food, medications, a flashlight, a battery radio and copies of important documents.
Sign up for alerts: text SHORESALERT to 555-0190.

Understanding the tides
There are 2 high tides and 2 low tides roughly every 24 hours and 50 minutes, so each day the tides are about 50 minutes later than the day before.
Spring tides, with the highest highs and lowest lows, come a day or two after a full or new moon. Neap tides, with the smallest range, fall in between. At Kittiwake Bay the range on a spring tide can be over 5 m.
The water rises fastest in the middle 2 hours of the flood. Always know when the tide turns before you walk out.

Posidonia: the meadows under the sea
The dark patches you see from the boat at Cala Serena are not rocks but meadows of Posidonia oceanica, a seagrass found only in the Mediterranean. A single meadow can be thousands of years old.
One square metre of Posidonia can produce up to 20 litres of oxygen a day, and its roots hold the sand in place, protecting the beaches from erosion.
Please help protect it: boats must anchor only on sand or use the 32 buoys provided, at €15 per night.
